column1: # VENDORED_EXCEPTIONS.tsv — intentional divergences from mojito-sys/native/
# Format: THREE TAB-separated fields per row, one row per diverged file:
#   <basename>    <sha256-of-vendored-file>    <reason>
# <basename>        the filename as it appears under vendor/mojito-sys/
#                   (e.g. native_stack.c, mojito_sys.h), OR, for a
#                   SPIKE-vs-PROD divergence (check-vendored.sh finding
#                   [4], issue #170 instance 6), `spike:<basename>` — the
#                   `spike:` prefix disambiguates from a finding [1]
#                   PROD-vs-canonical row of the same basename (e.g.
#                   native_stack.c has independent rows for each axis).
# <sha256>          sha256sum of the VENDORED copy — NOT the canonical copy.
#                   For a `spike:` row this is the SPIKE copy
#                   (spike/colorless_runtime/vendor/mojito-sys/<basename>),
#                   matching finding [4]'s framing of PROD as the
#                   authoritative side (Makefile:12 — the dylib is built
#                   from PROD only) and SPIKE as the one that drifted.
#                   Computed with: shasum -a 256 <file> | awk '{print $1}'
#                   check-vendored.sh refuses the row if the file's current
#                   hash differs, so a re-diverged file is caught automatically.
# <reason>          free-form prose explaining WHY this file deliberately
#                   diverges from canonical mojito-sys; include the PR/issue
#                   that introduced the divergence so future maintainers can
#                   trace the decision.
# Adding a row here is the declaration that the divergence is known and
# intentional.  It does NOT exempt the file from future drift checks: when
# the vendored file changes (re-vendor or local patch), the hash changes, the
# old row is rejected, and you must update the hash and reason.
# To record a new exception:
#   1. shasum -a 256 mojito_async/vendor/mojito-sys/<basename> | awk '{print $1}'
#   2. Add a row here: <basename>\t<hash>\t<reason>
#   3. Re-run check-vendored.sh to confirm the row is accepted.
# When all vendored files track canonical byte-for-byte, the correct
# representation of "no exceptions" is an empty data section (no data rows).
# Do not add a placeholder row; the absence of rows is the sentinel.
# Rows below record INTENTIONAL divergences for the vendored spike substrate.
# mojito-async uses the spike substrate by design until the frozen ABI
# integration is complete (sys#164).  When that integration lands, re-vendor
# from canonical mojito-sys/main and remove every row here.
# Files with a canonical counterpart that differ from it:
mjs_epoll.c
column3: intentional spike substrate; frozen ABI integration pending sys#164

column1: # SPIKE (spike/colorless_runtime/vendor/mojito-sys) against PROD
# (finding [4], issue #170 instance 6). Makefile:9-16 claims these two
# trees are byte-identical; they have not been since at least the A2.0
# M:N rework (issue #101) landed on PROD without a matching re-vendor of
# SPIKE, and nothing checked the claim before finding [4] existed.  PROD
# is authoritative (Makefile:12: the dylib links PROD's objects only;
# $(BUILD)/spike/%.o pattern rules exist but are never referenced by any
# target, so SPIKE's C has not actually been COMPILED by `make` for as
# long as this OBJS wiring has looked like this — a second, smaller
# instance of the same "the comment claims something the build graph
# doesn't do" pattern, filed as mojito-async#180 rather than fixed here).
spike:VENDORED_AT.txt
column3: provenance/prose-only file, expected to differ per copy (different vendor dates/paths); both copies also carried their own "byte-identical, diff -r is empty" claim, which was itself false the same way the Makefile's was — corrected in both copies in the same pass as this row (issue #170)

column1: spike:mojito_spike.h
column3: PROD's header gained ms_live_stack_count (oversubscription guard, EPIC #2/#101) that SPIKE's copy never received; SPIKE is a frozen A0 snapshot, not a live consumer of the newer stack-pool guard (issue #170)

column1: spike:native_stack.c
column3: SAFETY TRIPWIRE, read before ever re-linking SPIKE's objects: PROD's copy carries issue #145's g_registry_lock mutex (Bug 1: concurrent ms_stack_alloc/free/is_live) and ABA dead-list (Bug 2); SPIKE's copy has NEITHER. This is safe today ONLY because SPIKE's compiled objects are never linked into any dylib (see the OBJS note above) — SPIKE's own mojito_spike.mojo bindings resolve their externs against the PROD-built libmojito_spike.dylib at link time. If SPIKE ever becomes independently linked again, re-vendor this file from PROD FIRST (issue #170)
